newsitem.title: USA: NASD forms task force to aid criminal probes.
newsitem.headline: NASD forms task force to aid criminal probes.

text.p: The National Association of Securites Dealers disclosed Tuesday that it has formed a task force to coordinate securities probes with law enforcement officials.

"The task force will aid criminal authorities taking part in investigations and undercover operations involving the securities industry," Mary Schapiro, president of NASD Regulation, wrote in a Feb. 28 letter to Michigan Democrat Representative John Dingell.

"What we can bring to the criminal enforcement table is the necessary and technical expertise for government law enforcement agencies to conduct significant and effective criminal investigations," she wrote in the letter.
NASD is the self-regulatory agency that runs the Nasdaq stock market.

Last month, Dingell wrote to U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno and to the Securities and Exchange Commission and NASD to ask what they are doing about alleged organised crime infiltration of the small-capital stock market.
SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt later responded by giving Dingell -- the House Commerce Committee ranking member -- a confidential briefing on the allegations.

In the letter, Schapiro also offered a private briefing to discuss several ongoing senstive matters related to the NASD's work with the Organised Crime Unit of the FBI and other federal law enforcement agencies.
